He said to me: 'Increase in saying: O Allah, do not make me from the Mu'arreen, and do not remove me from Al-Taqsir.'

He said: 'Every deed you perform intending the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, be deficient in it in your own eyes, for all people, in their deeds, regarding what is between them and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are deficient.'

key_terms.الْمُعَارِينَ: The ones of temporary Eman (those whose faith may be revoked or who are tested)
key_terms.مُقَصِّرًا: Deficient (one who considers their deeds lacking)
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (intending His pleasure)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Al-Taqsir' in Shia supplications?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual nuance of 'Al-Taqsir' (deficiency) not as negligence, but as a conscious state of humility where the believer perceives their own righteous deeds as insufficient before the Divine. This concept aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'Ihsan' and the continuous self-assessment (muhasabah) of one's worship, ensuring that good deeds do not lead to spiritual arrogance. By asking to remain in 'Taqsir', the supplicant seeks to preserve the humility necessary for sincere devotion, recognizing that all human effort is inherently limited compared to Allah's perfection.
